### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **68** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1a399c0abe2b53038cd1b810f781fd426aff120b` — the merge of head `df09a1b979dfbadd6417fe19127a4c047811e6ae` into base `756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1a399c0abe2b53038cd1b810f781fd426aff120b && git checkout 1a399c0abe2b53038cd1b810f781fd426aff120b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26 df09a1b979dfbadd6417fe19127a4c047811e6ae && git checkout -B drift-repro 756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26 && git merge --no-ff df09a1b979dfbadd6417fe19127a4c047811e6ae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 756aba29a02c22c23d3a19a57b4f34046c3a2f26` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ee702119c1a9c640a7dcae71b22e50ba7bbeaaa6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: brief 6979408379; card #35138 (claim 6975089907, claim amendment 2 6976973578, os-dev report 6979330524 and area note 6979387847); PR #35198 (body and comments, the Docs Drift Check 6979326025 among them); the full diff against merge-base `ba6556c617` (13 files, +835/−45: 5 commits and the merge of `origin/main`); the changeset; and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only. `origin/main` has no commit since the merge-base that touches `packages/mcp`, `packages/core/src`, `packages/services/service-analytics/src` or `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`.

Face: the committed file list is one changeset plus files under `packages/core/src/`, `packages/mcp/src/`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/` and `packages/services/service-analytics/src/`. It touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path. `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` decides no face from the paths and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `yes (widening)`. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded on this head. So this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④. Every file is inside the file surface of amendment 2.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is still running.** 65 check-runs: 22 success, 11 skipped, 32 in progress, 0 failure. Still running: `Build Core`, `Test Core` (10 shards), `Test UI` (16 shards), `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Live E2E UI`. Complete and green: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · ESLint`, every `Lint ·` lane (among them `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, which carries the NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`), `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. I judge on what is complete. The seat must see the 32 running runs finish green on this head before landing.
- **The coded refusal is kept byte for byte: right.** `codedErrorResult` gains an optional second argument and renders `{ error }` exactly as before when it is absent. The `error` object is built by the same `dataDoorRefusalEnvelope` / `dataDoorAnswerOf` path as before, and the members are added beside it, never inside it. `dataDoorErrorResult` passes the members only on a refusal: a coded envelope, or a door answer that is not a server fault. `recordReadErrorResult` asks the schema only on that same condition, so a 5xx answer carries no member and costs no extra read. Every other caller of `dataDoorErrorResult` (the write tools and `delete_records`) passes no members, so their answers do not change.
- **When the members are present: right.** Only on a refused `query_records`, `aggregate_records` or `get_record`. `notRecorded` is `{ object }` when `describeObject` answers null, and `{ object, fields }` when it shows the object but not some of the sent names. Names are deduplicated and kept in the order first sent. A served object whose fields are all shown, a schema read that throws, and a schema answer with no field list all give no member. `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are always counted as shown. That is correct, because the engine answers them on every object and a schema need not list them. A read that answers is untouched, because the catch is never reached. The `get_record` miss on a served object sends no field names, so it carries no member and stays a plain `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Built only from the sent names and the served schema: right, at rule level.** `notRecordedMembersOf` reads two things: the names the caller sent (`objectName`, and the field names gathered from `where`, `fields`, `orderBy`, `groupBy` and each aggregation's `field` and `filter`) and `bridge.describeObject`, which is the `describe_object` answer for this caller on both doors. The refusal's code, message and status do not take part in the members. `ifNotRecorded` is one constant sentence per language, and it names nothing. So nothing the served schema shows is named or counted, and an object or field the caller cannot see gets members that are byte-identical to those for one that does not exist. The CONTROL pins in `mcp-not-recorded.test.ts` compare the members across three refusal kinds for a field and for an object. `runtime/src/domains/mcp-not-recorded.test.ts` checks, over the real security layer on the HTTP bridge, that the served schema shows neither a denied field nor an unknown one, and that `describeObject` answers null for an object the caller cannot read, as it does for an unknown name. On the stdio door, `describeObject` reads the caller's view (`callerObjectView` at `origin/main`). That view treats an object the principal may not read as a name it does not hold, and it projects out any field the principal cannot read. So the same rule holds there, read but not pinned (N2).
- **Gathering the sent names: right in `where`, too wide elsewhere (S1).** `whereFieldNames` goes into `$and`, `$or`, `$nor` and `$not`, skips every other `$` key and reads a dotted key by its head. Entries in `fields`, `orderBy`, `groupBy` and an aggregation's `field` are taken whole, so a dotted entry there is named as a whole string (S1).
- **`pickSentenceLocale` and `platformLocaleNamedBy` in `@objectstack/core`: right, and the move does not change behaviour.** `platformLocaleNamedBy` is the `service-analytics` function moved verbatim. `pickSentenceLocale` is the old loop, generic over the languages a producer writes. `datasetToolSentenceLocale` now passes `Object.keys(COPY)`, which is the same set as the old `hasOwnProperty` test against `COPY`, and keeps its signature and return type. `@objectstack/service-analytics` already depends on `@objectstack/core`, and `@objectstack/core` already depends on `@objectstack/spec`. No other export of `@objectstack/core` uses either name. Ablations show the service-analytics locale pins and the new core prefix pin both turn red without the picker.
- **`userTextLocales()` on both bridges: right.** `McpDataBridge` gains an optional member, so an existing implementer still compiles. The HTTP bridge answers `userTextLocalesOf(ec)`, the request's ladder. The stdio bridge answers the principal's ladder and then the i18n service's default. A throwing or missing i18n service adds no rung. A missing member, or one that throws, is answered in `en`. The tripwire and stored-metadata rosters each list the member once, and it reads no record.
- **What the built entries reach: nothing removed, renamed or narrowed.** `@objectstack/core`'s `.` entry gains two exports. `@objectstack/mcp`'s entry gains an optional member on the exported `McpDataBridge` type. `NotRecordedMembers` and the widened `codedErrorResult` stay module-level and are not on the entry. `@objectstack/runtime`'s bridge object gains one member. In `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `datasetToolSentenceLocale` is unchanged, and the function that moved out was module-private. Every input accepted before is still accepted, and every member answered before is still answered.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no data query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. A refused read now makes one schema read and one locale read, and only when it was refused.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix): a dotted entry outside `where` is named as not recorded, and the sentence then misleads.** `whereFieldNames` reads `owner.region` by its head, `owner`. But `queryRecordsSentFields` and `aggregateRecordsSentFields` take `fields`, `orderBy`, `groupBy` and an aggregation's `field` whole. Since #7589, the engine refuses a dotted projection with `INVALID_FIELD` 400 (`assertProjectionHasNoDottedPaths`, `engine-top-level.ts` at `origin/main`). That refusal's message tells the caller to name the whole column. So `query_records` with `fields` set to `owner.name`, on an object whose `owner` lookup the caller is served, now answers `notRecorded` naming `owner.name`. The `ifNotRecorded` sentence then tells the model to report the data as not recorded and not to answer with another field. That is the wrong answer this card exists to prevent, and it contradicts the remedy given in the refusal beside it. A dotted `orderBy` entry has the same effect whenever the read is refused for another reason. To close it, read every sent name by its head, as `where` does (or leave dotted names out). Then add one pin with a dotted `fields` entry on a served lookup. The security rule is not affected: a dotted name is still built only from what was sent. The original reviewer reads the delta.
- **N1 (nit): the core jsdoc says more than is true.** The jsdoc on `pickSentenceLocale` says it is "ONE picker for every executor that hands a caller a finished sentence". Other copies of the same table lookup remain at `origin/main`: `platformLocaleNamedBy` in `packages/lint/src/finding-user-text.ts`, which does not depend on core, and `driverCatalogLocaleOf` in `@objectstack/service-datasource`. The changeset states the scope correctly: the dataset tools and the MCP record tools. Prose only.
- **N2 (nit): the stdio door's half of the rule is read, not pinned.** The runtime pin covers the HTTP bridge over the real security layer. On stdio, only `userTextLocales` is pinned. I read that the stdio `describeObject` follows the same rule (①). A stdio twin of the runtime pin's schema and refusal checks would keep it held. The code is right today, so this has no correctness or contract effect.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/35138-mcp-not-recorded.md`: right.** It bumps `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/service-analytics` at `patch`. Those are exactly the four published packages whose source changes. A new public export of `@objectstack/core` is a widening outside the metadata protocol. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says that `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and that a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. CI `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** It starts its line in both the PR body and the changeset, and the arm is from the closed pair. New answer members present only on a refused read, a new optional bridge member and two new exports are all widenings. No input is newly refused, and nothing is removed or renamed. Claim 6975089907 and amendment 2 declared `Clause-②: yes`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The type stays local to `packages/mcp`, and the sentence lives in the executor (ADR-0149 M1).
- **Changeset prose against the diff: right, with S1.**
  - "the refusal now carries two members beside it, on the HTTP and the stdio server alike": one handler in `registerObjectTools`, two bridges.
  - "for the field names the call sent that the schema does not show, in the order sent": true. For a dotted name outside `where`, this is the S1 case.
  - "both members are built from the names the caller sent and from the caller's served schema, and nothing else": true (①).
  - "The refusal itself (`isError`, its `code`, `message` and `status`) is unchanged, byte for byte": true.
  - "A read that answers, a refusal about a field the caller's schema shows, a server fault, and a refusal whose schema read cannot be made carry no member": true, where every name sent is one the schema shows.
  - "`id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` ... are never named": true.
  - "The dataset tools' `nextStep` and `sourceLine` ... use the same picker, with unchanged behaviour": true. Both go through `datasetToolSentenceLocale`.
  - "the HTTP bridge answers the request's ladder, the stdio bridge the principal's ladder and then the i18n service's default. A bridge without it is answered in `en`": true.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (a description sentence and an ask-card question for the members): answered A in 6979387847. It becomes a follow-up PR on #35138 under its own amendment, after this PR lands. This PR stays as it is.
- Out-of-scope note (the same two items, carrier #35138): answered by the same follow-up.
- Deviation, the stdio locale ladder reads the principal's ladder before the i18n default: answered in 6979387847 and right. It keeps `nextStep` and `ifNotRecorded` in one language for one stdio caller, and the pin covers both rungs.
- Deviation, the members do not depend on the refusal's code: answered and right. This is how the rule is met (①).
- Deviation, the test-double edit in `stdio-data-bridge.not-found.test.ts`: answered. The HTTP twin now serves `task` from `describeObject`, as the stdio side does. Without that, a record miss there would read as an unknown object and break the PARITY pin. Test only.
- Deviation, model-free commit trailers: process only.
- NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: answered. CI `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries it and succeeded on this head.
- NOT-MEASURED `check:type-check-debt` at the merge head (local timeout): answered. CI `Type Check · debt ledger` succeeded on this head.
- `security_findings: withheld`: answered in 6979387847, which says the seat handles it outside this record. It is not judged here.
- Ablations: ten mutations, each turned a pin red and was restored to the HEAD blob. The core prefix ablation first stayed green, and the dev added prefix-only codes until it went red. No ablation covers dotted names (S1) or the stdio schema (N2).
- Overlap: #35193 (#35144, area o1-C) conflicts textually in `mcp-http-tools.ts`, the tripwire test and `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`. Whichever lands second merges `main`, and the merge queue re-tests the result.
- Docs: no page in `content/docs` states the error body of these three tools, so no page becomes untrue. The follow-up for the description sentence is the right carrier.
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), assignee `os-warren`, so no extra author note is owed. S1 needs a new head, and the original reviewer reads the delta. Before landing, the seat must also see the 32 running runs finish green on the final head (①).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `df09a1b979dfbadd6417fe19127a4c047811e6ae`
Local-runs: none

Delta review: record 6979581416 on `ee702119c1` gave PASS with S1 open and nits N1 and N2. This delta covers that head to this one. Inputs: the delta `ee702119c1..df09a1b979` (3 commits, no merge of `main`, 4 files: the changeset, `packages/core/src/sentence-locale.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/mcp-not-recorded.test.ts`), the round-2 os-dev report 6981260016, and this head's check-runs. Code outside the delta was read at `origin/main` only.

Face: unchanged. The delta touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path, and the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` lines in the changeset are unchanged. So this is still the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is complete and green.** 68 check-runs: 57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress. `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Build Core`, every `Type Check ·` lane and every `Lint ·` lane succeeded. `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries the dev's NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, and it succeeded.
- **S1: closed.** `notRecordedMembersOf` now maps every sent name through `sentFieldHead` (the first path segment) before comparing it with the served schema. It drops an empty head, then deduplicates in the order first sent. Every channel goes through this one place: `where` (which now pushes the whole key), `fields`, `orderBy`, `groupBy`, and each aggregation's `field` and `filter`. A dotted name whose head the schema shows now gives no member. A dotted name whose head the schema does not show names only the head. The new pin covers all six channels with a served head, plus one unknown head. The dev's ablation (whole names restored) turned five pins red.
- **The rule still holds after the change.** The members are still built only from the sent names (now their heads) and the caller's served schema. A head is a prefix of the caller's own string. Nothing after the first dot is ever named. So nothing the schema shows is named, and a name the caller cannot see still gets the same members as one that does not exist.
- **N2: closed.** The stdio twin runs the real `createStdioDataBridge`, its own caller view and the real `registerObjectTools` over the shared ADR-0106 case table (`OBJECT_SCHEMA_MASK_CASES` with its `securityDoubleFor`). For every field case and every object case with masking on, the members for what the caller cannot see equal, byte for byte, the members for a name that does not exist (with the name swapped). A field the caller can see, and a dotted name through it, give no member. The dev's second ablation (stdio `describeObject` served the declared object instead of the caller's view) turned the three field cases red. I agree with area answer A: the twin pins the stdio door's schema half on the table every object-schema exit is judged by. The runtime twin already covers the real security layer on the HTTP door, and adding a `plugin-security` devDependency is outside the file surface. Both test imports already resolve: `@objectstack/metadata-core` (its `./testing` entry, which three other stdio test files in `packages/mcp` already import) and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` are dependencies of `@objectstack/mcp`. The twin's engine double now carries only `find`, `count` and `aggregate`. Removing `findOne` is test-only, and `Lint · ESLint` succeeded.
- **N1: closed.** The `pickSentenceLocale` jsdoc now names its two consumers, the dataset tools and the MCP record tools, and no longer claims every executor.
- **Built entries: nothing new.** `sentFieldHead` is module-private. No export, signature or answer key changes in the delta. `whereFieldNames` is still module-private, and its names reach the members only through `notRecordedMembersOf`, where `sentFieldHead` applies.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The delta adds no data read.

### ② Semver level

- **Unchanged and right.** The changeset still bumps the same four packages at `patch` with the same two declaration lines. `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **The changeset's new sentence matches the code.** It says every sent name is read by its head on all six channels, and that a dotted name whose head the schema shows is never named.
- **The PR body is one round behind (N3).** Its "What changes" bullet can still be read as head-reading `where` only. Its quick-read and Tests sections still count 14 cases in `mcp-not-recorded.test.ts`, where this head has 22. The changeset is what ships, and it matches this head. The PR body ships nothing and does not hold the declaration lines that changed, since they did not change. This is the prose face only.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, the stdio twin runs on the case table's security double, not the real SecurityPlugin: answered (area A, ① N2). Accepted.
- Deviation, the PR body is not edited: N3.
- NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: answered by CI on this head (①).
- `security_findings: withheld`: unchanged. The seat handles it outside this record.
- Overlap: #35193 still conflicts in the same three files. The dev reports this round did not change that, and whoever lands second merges `main`.
- Findings: No must-fix, no should-fix. One new nit:
  - **N3 (nit, prose face):** the PR body's member description and test counts describe round 1. The seat may update the body without moving the head. It has no correctness or contract effect.
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), so no extra author note is owed. Only a nit remains, so this is the final round unless the head moves for a reason other than prose.

## Final head for L1 · 2026-11-18T14:23Z

Head-sha: `df09a1b979` · all check-runs success or skipped (57 success, 11 skipped, 0 red; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` carries the locally NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) · NOT governed, +1015 / −45.
